numerical_failure.observed_behavior: In the test test_enet_ols_consistency, the ordering assertion se_enet <= se_ols <= 1e-20 fails (e.g. local run: assert 7.304604230718523e-26 <= 6.721669301829635e-26); the squared error is computed without sample_weight even though both models are fit with sample_weight, and tight absolute tolerances on intercept_ fail for some seeds near zero.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: No test failures: ElasticNet with alpha=0 (Ridge-like) should give predictions and coefficients matching OLS within the test tolerances (assert_allclose on predict, coef_ with atol=1e-11, intercept_ with atol=1e-12) and the squared-error ordering should hold.
trigger_conditions: Net(alpha=0, precompute=precompute, tol=1e-15).fit(X, y, sample_weight=sw) with alpha=0 (no L1 penalty)
precompute is False or True as parametrized in test_enet_ols_consistency
specific seeds such as 42 (e.g. test_enet_ols_consistency[42-10-False]) and 59 (test_enet_ols_consistency[59-None-True]) when run across multiple seeds with SKLEARN_TESTS_GLOBAL_RANDOM_SEED=all
intercept comparisons near zero with tight absolute tolerance

oracle_clues: Reference CI failure in Azure build 83843
PR#32845 fix made CD converge for alpha=0 by using alternative dual gap; the new test_enet_ols_consistency documents surprising results

numerical_characteristics.precision: rtol=1e-5 when precompute=True and rtol=1e-7 otherwise for coef_ comparison in the Ridge-vs-ElasticNet(l1_ratio=0) test; the gram-matrix (precompute=True) CD solver is noted to lose numerical precision by working with squares like Q=X'X
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: make_regression with n_samples=300, n_features=100, effective_rank in {None, 10}; sample weights drawn uniformly from [0.01, 10]; test asserts se_enet <= 1e-20 (squared residuals) for OLS consistency
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: tol=1e-11 if ridge_alpha >= 1e-2 else 1e-16 for ElasticNet convergence in the Ridge comparison test; tol=1e-15 in test_enet_ols_consistency; assert_allclose atol=1e-11 for coef_ and atol=1e-12 for intercept_ in OLS consistency test
category_specific_evidence: Coordinate descent (CD) solver with dual gap stopping criterion does not converge for alpha=0 / l1_ratio=0 (Ridge-like) because the dual gap is not valid there (PR#32845).

Fix adds dual_gap_formulation_A in _cd_fast.pyx computing primal minus dual with a rescaled dual point (scale = alpha/dual_norm_XtA if dual_norm_XtA > alpha, else 1.0), and an alternative dual gap (formulation B) for MultiTaskElasticNet.
Issue #32987 reports test_enet_ols_consistency failing with assertions on squared errors near 1e-25/1e-26 scale, e.g. 7.3e-26 <= 6.7e-26, for precompute True/False and effective_rank None/10.
Original test used warning suppression for ConvergenceWarning which was removed once convergence was achieved; the new test uses filterwarnings for 'With alpha=0, this algorithm' UserWarning.
Ridge comparison test chooses ElasticNet alpha = ridge_alpha / sw.sum() (sample-weighted) or ridge_alpha / n_samples (MultiTaskElasticNet, which does not support sample weights).
Precision loss with gram matrix: R^2 = y^2 + wQw - 2yQw is cited as the reason precompute=True needs looser rtol.
reproduction_risks: Failing cases are seed-dependent (parametrized with global_random_seed, e.g. [42-10-False], [59-None-True]), so results vary across random seeds.
Absolute squared-error assertions near 1e-20 to 1e-26 are sensitive to floating-point round-off and BLAS backend (passage environment shows openblas 0.3.25, numpy 1.24.1, scipy 1.10.0).
Iteration count at which behaviour differs is not stated in the passages.
Initialisation of coefficients for the CD solver is not stated in the passages.
Stopping criterion detail: passages say the dual gap is invalid at alpha=0 but do not give the exact stopping test or max_iter value.
